digest.component_or_area: rebar reconciler: inbound-probe dispatch chain and deletion handling
propositions: The (inbound, probe) dispatch chain has no live producer: differ._compute_mutations_emit_absent_partner_probes only emits when it sees jira_key-bearing local_state, but run_differs passes a fetched Jira snapshot whose entries carry no jira_key, so the producer never fires in production.

The deletion-vs-aged-out discrimination that ADR 0028 para 2 relies on IS implemented elsewhere and live: outbound_differ._safe_get_issue and binding_walk both perform bounded direct GETs and map 404 to confirmed deletion, verified on real DC.

When a Jira issue is confirmed deleted (3x 404), the binding is retired and popped from both bindings and reverse, leaving the local ticket unbound; outbound_differ then creates a fresh Jira issue, resurrecting the deleted work after a 3-pass delay.
Prior art (Unito, Kubernetes reconcilers) rejects automatic resurrection of deliberately-deleted work items, treating absent objects as gone rather than subjects for re-creation.

The decision is to delete the dead legacy chain (producer, dispatch arm, inbound_probe.py, route_inbound_probe) and add a tombstone guard that suppresses outbound-create for any local ticket with a retired binding, preventing resurrection while allowing unretire as an escape hatch.
